eval.title: Is SBUX Stock A Great Business At A Fair Price Now?

call.headline_quote: so Starbucks yes it is a relative buy it is an okay absolute buy it is not a value investing bargain

base_metric.name: net_income
base_metric.quote: 20 5 billion of revenues in 2019 I still see growth there and also increased profitability

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: going forward in 10 years I get to 8 billion and a p ratio of 12 if they keep on growing the p ratio will remain at 20 or 25 and you got yourself a 7% return Plus 2.5% dividend and easily 10% return from buying Starbucks now

scenarios.name: best
scenarios.quote: we see that they estimate 14 16 177% growth in earnings in their models over the next three years if that happens and Starbucks reaches higher levels

what_is_priced_in.quote: especially at the Pu ratio in line with the market which is 25

reasons.claim: Comparable sales, store growth and improving operating margins are driving 20% EPS growth even amid temporary headwinds.
reasons.quote: their earnings per share are growing at 20% and the Global store count is higher by 7% 38,000 stores and they say there is plenty more room for growth

data_check.gap_note: he says 20, as-of 3.58 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: store count growth

reasons.claim: At a P/E of 15 the stock is a relative and okay absolute buy but not a true value-investing bargain with sufficient margin of safety.
reasons.quote: however from a value investing perspective I would need a better margin of safety from that valuation perspective

data_check.gap_note: he says 15, as-of 25.5279 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition

reasons.claim: Near-term demand is being hit by Middle East-related boycotts and softer US customer visit frequency.
reasons.quote: negative impact from the Middle East also impact in the US and this is something that we have to discuss here so specifically us customers who tend to visit India afternoon came in less frequently

reasons.claim: China remains a large runway with thousands of cities still to penetrate, supporting long-term store growth.
reasons.quote: they still have 2,000 and more cities in China to penetrate and therefore there is still room for growth

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: China store growth target

reasons.claim: Analyst estimates are even more exuberant than his own base case, implying meaningfully higher returns if realized.
reasons.quote: we see that they estimate 14 16 177% growth in earnings in their models over the next three years

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: analyst earnings growth estimate

external_facts_used: Analyst consensus estimates of 14-17% earnings growth over the next three years
Conference call commentary on Middle East boycott and lower US afternoon customer visits
Target of penetrating 2,000+ additional cities in China
Comparison to JD Peet's coffee company's debt levels, P/E of 26, and declining net income

critic.notes: Reason 2 misstates: P/E 15 is his hypothetical value-buy level, not the current P/E (~25). Reason 3's 'boycotts' isn't stated, only 'negative impact from the Middle East'.
